title: Short recurrent flag episodes fit 8,772 TESS sectors without a lower bound of 18 years on material life
abstract: We test whether long persistence of complex periodic variable host status requires long material or supply episodes. We fit the released 1,746 clean stars, 8,772 sectors and 245 flags with three fixed recurrence types. All types have positive duty. The best fit has mean on times of 24.9, 36.5 and 103.3 days and log likelihood -627.623, compared with -631.161 for the source permanent-host mixture. A covariance proof shows that fixed differences in duty produce long memory after short episode memory has ended. A finite-sample bound shows that very rare recurrence cannot be separated uniformly from zero duty. The age decline remains in the weight of frequent stars. A crowding cut removes the rare-class improvement; reducing efficiency lengthens one mean on time to 1.49 years. Thus rare physical events are not established. The source host-time bound remains conditional on its model, but it does not bound material life. Flags are threshold states, not measurements of cloud identity. Code, aggregate fits, tests and exact source hashes are included.
